open_points.subject: Models M30–M34 model kind and emitted identity
open_points.text:
On 2026-11-27 five correspondences over a closed list that the data
provider held as text-to-text maps became tables whose rows name the
members themselves (SPEC_STANDARD §15.2, "a correspondence over a
taxonomy"), so their rows have the records M30–M34 (owner, 2026-11-27).
open_points.question: Are M30–M34 ordinary value models for individual rows, read-only models with kind mapping/catalog, or ordinary row models accompanied by separate mapping/catalog models for the five tables?
options: M30–M34 are ordinary value row models and are emitted as runtime dataclasses
M30–M34 are the read-only mapping/catalog models and therefore have kind instead of identity
M30–M34 are ordinary row models, and five additional mapping/catalog models represent the tables
open_points.default_guess: Treat M30–M34 as ordinary value row models and represent the provider tables separately as read-only spec data.

witness.initial: State 6 translates the five new State 1 records into the specification's models section.
events: The compiler processes M30–M34 and the data provider constants.
Generated code imports or constructs a row from one of the five tables.
outcomes: M30–M34 are emitted runtime dataclasses with value identity, so the row type exists in generated code.
M30–M34 are mapping/catalog spec data, so no corresponding runtime row class reaches generated code.
witness.observer: Generated modules and any contract or provider implementation that names a row type

open_points.subject: FormFieldRefusalKind readers
open_points.text:
A row of the form refusal table: the kind of refusal a value outside its form
is answered with, by the form field it was given as — a field of a
closed list answers `outside_closed_list`, every other field `outside_form`.
open_points.question: Which product actions and forms must read FORM_FIELD_REFUSAL_KINDS when producing a refusal?
options: Every owner-interface form validation that uses a FormField
Only actions explicitly assigned this table in a later contract
open_points.default_guess: Use it for every product form validation whose rejected input is classified by FormField.

witness.initial: The owner submits an out-of-form value for a non-closed-list field through a form other than the import form.
outcomes: The action reads FORM_FIELD_REFUSAL_KINDS and answers `outside_form`.
The action does not read the table because only import or a later-selected subset of forms uses it.

open_points.subject: ImportFormFailureField table contents
open_points.text:
A row of the import form failure table: the field of the import mapping a
value's form failure is reported under, by the form field the value was
checked as (R0-85) — an alias under the alias, a customer kind under the
customer kind. One row for each form field the import checks.
open_points.question: What is the closed set of import-checked form fields, and what MappingField corresponds to each one beyond the two correspondences named in the passage?
options: The table has exactly the two named rows: alias to alias and customer kind to customer kind
Every field validated by import has a row, including any fields not named here
Only failures that can be returned to the owner have rows
open_points.default_guess: Include exactly the two named rows unless another State 1 model explicitly enumerates further import-checked form fields.

witness.initial: An imported project contains an invalid value in an import-checked form field other than alias or customer kind.
events: The owner uploads and confirms the import.
Registry detects the field's form failure.
Registry selects the MappingField under which to report it.
outcomes: The table contains a row for that field, and the failure is reported under its mapped import field.
The table contains only the two named rows, leaving no model fact that selects a reporting field.
witness.observer: The owner reviewing the refused import

open_points.subject: CustomerEligibilityRefusal correspondence values
open_points.text:
A row of the customer eligibility refusal table: the kind of refusal a
project's customer is refused with, by the customer's eligibility — an
erased, restricted or ended customer (R0-16, R0-51, R0-57).
open_points.question: Which RefusalKind value corresponds to each of erased, restricted and ended eligibility?
options: Each eligibility maps to its own distinct RefusalKind
All three eligibilities map to one common customer-ineligible RefusalKind
Some eligibilities share a RefusalKind and others use distinct kinds
open_points.default_guess: Map erased, restricted and ended eligibility to distinct refusal kinds.

witness.initial: A project create or correction tries to newly name an ended customer.
events: Registry refuses the attempted customer assignment.
Registry selects the refusal kind from CUSTOMER_ELIGIBILITY_REFUSALS.
outcomes: The answer carries a refusal kind specific to an ended relationship.
The answer carries a common refusal kind shared by all ineligible customers.
witness.observer: The owner or service receiving the refusal

open_points.subject: CustomerEligibilityRefusal action coverage
open_points.text:
One row for each eligibility
that refuses; an eligible customer and an unknown one have none.
open_points.question: Which actions must read CUSTOMER_ELIGIBILITY_REFUSALS: project creation, project correction, migration import, or every action that newly assigns a customer?
options: Every action that newly assigns a customer reads it
Only ordinary project creation and correction read it
Only the later contracts that explicitly name the table read it
open_points.default_guess: Use it for every action that newly assigns an existing customer, including create and correction; do not apply it to import-created customer records unless import assigns an already-existing customer.

witness.initial: An action attempts to newly assign a restricted existing customer to a project.
events: The action resolves the Customer record.
The action decides whether to consult CUSTOMER_ELIGIBILITY_REFUSALS.
outcomes: The action reads the table and returns its eligibility-specific refusal.
The action does not read the table because its action category was not specified here, and it follows separate or later-defined behavior.
